newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed down on Friday but off their session lows, having largely recovered from the release of stronger than expected U.S. economic data.
"We came off quite sharply in the first instance after the macro figures, but we've recovered quite well," a dealer said.
"The market is basically quite well supported," agreed another dealer, citing buying on dips.
Dealers agreed the short- to medium range was well-bid, adding that the undertone up to 2002s was good, with some swapping out of equivalent bunds.
News that the Chicago Purchasing Managers index rose to 60.0 in August from 51.2 in July took the market by surprise, sending both U.S. Treasuries and German bunds lower.
The Dutch 10-year January 2006 benchmark extended losses in late trade to close down 17 points at 97.81/89 for a bid yield of 6.30 pct vs 6.28 pct on Thursday.
But the yield spread versus the April 2006 bund widened to nine basis points, prompting some dealers to predict a double-digit guilder to bund discount in the near-term.
The recent steepening of the yield curve eased off, with flattening in the five to ten-year range.
Dealers said the long end was more cautious, with Jan 2023s closing at 106.46/66 for a bid yield of 6.95, 17 basis points under long bunds versus 18 on Thursday.
